label: D2 after choosing a1, early in the episode
explanation: Fires only at D2 (never D1/GO). 93% of mass comes from steps where the just-made choice (in_action) was a1, and it is mostly at S1. Its rate and magnitude drop steadily with the trial index in the episode (rate 0.26 for trials 0-9, 0.06 for 50-59, essentially 0 from trial 60 on), so it acts like an a1-at-D2 detector that is gated by time in the episode. In the examples magnitude is highest for a1 followed by common S1, lower for a1 followed by rare S2 (~0.65-0.7 of max), and lower again for a2 with S2 (~0.5). It does not fire when reward input is 1, which is never the case at D2 anyway. All variables are observed at D2. Dev scores: F1 0.84, mass recall 0.93. Cutting at ep_trial < 55 gives F1 0.86; I kept 60 as the simpler cut. Adding state==1 as an alternative to a1 raises recall but costs precision.

issues: The main claims hold. Dev: the feature fires only at D2 (D1 and GO both 0/380619), 92.7% of its activation mass is at in_action = a1, and the firing rate falls with ep_trial (0.26 for trials 0-9, 0.061 for 50-59, 0.001 for 60-69, then 0). Test scores reproduce exactly: P 0.835, R 0.838, F1 0.836, mass recall 0.923.

There is a systematic miss class: a2 followed by a rare transition to S1, early in the episode. The predicate (D2 & action==2 & state==1 & ep_trial<20) has dev precision 0.92 and covers 8.2% of active steps. The explanation never mentions this case. Its own magnitude ordering (a2 reaching S2 at about 0.5) leaves it out.

There is a second miss class: on the first few trials (ep_trial < 4), a2 reaching S2 also fires reliably (precision 0.80). Together with the case above, this is most of the 17315 test-split misses. The test-split misses are dominated by a2 windows with good=S1 or low_first, which looks like a structured gap rather than scattered noise.

The label is time-gated in a coarse way. With a1 at D2, precision is 0.999 for trials 0-9, 0.72 for trials 40-49 and only 0.40 for trials 50-59. So the feature is a steadily decaying signal, not a step at 60. A cut at 50 gives dev P 0.93 and F1 0.84.

Some contingencies that are not in the label: given the predicate, rare a1 (reaching S2) has precision 0.61 and common a1 has 0.91. The firing rate is higher when S1 started good (start_high 0.112 vs 0.067) and when good=S1 (0.141 vs 0.030). These are secondary modulations.
No future variables are involved. The original and the improved predicate both use only phase, the agent's own choice, the reached state (observed at D2) and ep_trial.
